cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls the contest and A5 selects a favorable judge, but A3 generic question delay does not enact approval of B cost challenge.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cheaper-dinner condition informs A3 free-potato claim; B4 voucher informs A5 taste contest, despite the irrelevant A3 preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 pursue a practical meal and price constraint, making A competitive reinterpretation responsive.

heightening.evidence: B4 ties the price and A5 changes the winning criterion to taste with a biased judge.
